ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, as amended by Real Decreto-ley 7/2021, de 27 de abril, transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010; Real Decreto 229/2023, de 30 de marzo, por el que se aprueba el Reglamento de desarrollo de la Ley 10/2010; and relevant provisions of Ley 6/2023, de 17 de marzo, de los Mercados de Valores y de los Servicios de Inversión concerning the central UBO registers.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / corporate existence of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identification card of each shareholder, director, and appointed representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent issuing authority in the country of nationality or residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy plus Hague Apostille where required, followed by sworn Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of no criminal record (certificado de antecedentes penales) of each proposed administrator

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, administrators, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against Spanish, EU, UN, OFAC, and equivalent consolidated sanctions lists, as well as Spanish, EU, and international PEP databases, prior to incorporation. The notary and the licensed corporate service provider must conduct risk-based due diligence in accordance with Articles 3-10 of Ley 10/2010 and retain all documentary evidence for a period of ten years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) - Certificado de Denominación Social online service at registradores.org
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed denomination must be written in Castilian Spanish or in any co-official Spanish language using Latin script. Foreign words in Latin alphabet are permissible only if clearly readable, not misleading, and not contrary to Spanish legal order. The name must exactly match the certificate issued by the Registro Mercantil Central; no translation or transliteration is permitted at registration. For a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada, the name must be followed by 'Sociedad Limitada', 'S.L.', or 'S.L' as approved by the registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registro Mercantil Central rejects the proposed denomination due to identity or similarity with an existing name, the applicant may immediately submit a new denomination certificate request for an alternative name. The applicant may also file an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (formerly Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado) within one month of notification of the rejection, attaching the denial notification, the original certificate request, and legal arguments demonstrating that the name does not infringe any statutory prohibition.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office is not accepted as the sole registered office of a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada. The registered office must be a genuine physical address in Spain where the company's legal representative is accessible, the tax domicile can be evidenced, and the books and records of the company may be inspected. For the low-risk digital MMORPG publishing industry, remote administrative operations are tolerated, but a virtual office may only serve as a supplementary mail-forwarding address and not as statutory registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 20% to 30% during the first three years of operation, with an elevated risk if the registered office is shared with a virtual-office provider or a gestoría, as Spanish registrars and tax authorities actively inspect shell-company substance indicators.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market-benchmarked professional compliance fee for pre-incorporation due diligence

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Spain – Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC), particularly Articles 4 (minimum capital), 12-13 (articles of association), 19-21 (constitution), 22-30 (founder formalities), 31-36 (nullity and defects), 58-60 (deed of incorporation), 62-63 (registered office and corporate purpose), 67 (registration and publicity), 74 (paid-up capital) and 209-216 (administration). Supplementary instruments: Law 14/2013 of 27 September on support for entrepreneurs and their internationalization (CIRCE and DUE electronic incorporation), Law 18/2022 of 17 October on the creation and growth of companies (1-euro SL and expedited incorporation), Royal Decree 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil) and Royal Decree 2/2021.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) for name certification and BORME publication; Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office for the constitutive inscription; CIRCE (Centro de Información y Red de Creación de Empresas) as the electronic gateway; Notary of the Colegio Notarial for the deed; Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) for NIF and census filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (public notarial deed of incorporation) transmitted electronically through the Single Electronic Document (Documento Único Electrónico – DUE) via CIRCE, followed by inscription in the Registro Mercantil Provincial and publication in the BORME.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The statutory minimum capital for an SL is EUR 3,000 (Art. 4 LSC), fully subscribed and fully paid-up at constitution. Law 18/2022 permits incorporation with a nominal capital of EUR 1, provided that the legal reserve and distribution-restriction rules of Art. 4.5 LSC are observed until the accumulated reserves plus capital equal EUR 3,000. Cash contributions must be evidenced by a bank certificate dated not more than two months before the deed or paid directly to the notary; in-kind contributions are admissible. No escrow account is mandated by national law, though founders commonly deposit funds in a temporary bank account designated for the company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, (i) that the notarial deed of incorporation and the articles of association are approved in their entirety; (ii) that the subscribed share capital of EUR 3,000 is fully paid by the founding shareholders, as evidenced in the deed; (iii) that the registered office is fixed at Calle Hermosilla 10, 28001 Madrid, Spain; (iv) that, effective upon inscription in the Mercantile Registry, [Full Name] is appointed Sole Director (Administrador Único) with full powers of representation and management; (v) that the Sole Director is authorized to obtain the provisional Tax Identification Number, open bank accounts, and execute the registration with the Mercantile Registry and all ancillary filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the official negative name certificate (certificación negativa de denominación social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) – online portal CIRCE (www.circe.es) or the Colegio de Registradores de la Propiedad y Mercantiles de España.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the electronic name-certificate application through CIRCE or at the Registro Mercantil Central, indicating the desired Spanish corporate name of the SL and up to four alternative names. Pay the certification fee and download the electronically sealed certificate. The certificate is valid for three months and must be presented to the notary; in electronic incorporation it is embedded in the DUE dossier.
required_dossiers: Name application form (Solicitud de certificación negativa de denominación) with up to 5 proposed names
DNI, NIE or passport of the applicant or legal representative
Power of attorney when filing on behalf of non-resident or corporate founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar objects to the proposed denomination because of identity or confusion with an existing company (Art. 407 RRM), file an amended application within the same electronic procedure using the reference number of the initial request, or attach written authorization from the proprietary company, or select a new distinctive name. The amended certificate is re-issued without additional cost.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the notarial deed of incorporation (escritura de constitución) with full payment of capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Notary (Notario) of the Colegio Notarial selected by the founders; in the CIRCE electronic procedure the system assigns the notary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Attend the notary appointment, physically or through an appointed attorney-in-fact, with the valid name certificate, draft articles of association and proof of payment of the capital. The capital contribution is made in cash to the notary or previously to a Spanish bank account with a certificate dated within two months before the deed. The notary verifies legal capacity and legality, adapts the articles, requests the provisional NIF from AEAT, signs the deed, and transmits it electronically to the Registro Mercantil Provincial within two working days.
required_dossiers: Certificación negativa de denominación social (valid name certificate)
Bank certificate of capital deposit dated not more than 2 months before the deed, or proof of cash paid to the notary
Identity documents (DNI/NIE/passport) of all founder shareholders and directors
NIF of non-resident shareholders and, if applicable, notarial power of attorney for the founding act
Beneficial ownership declaration (declaración de titularidad real) for the Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses execution because of defective name certificate, capital, or capacity, rectify the defects within five working days and reschedule; if a Registry defect note is anticipated, the notary corrects the deed before signing. The DUE system permits resubmission within two weeks without losing the original reference data.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – state tax administration agency; portal: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident entity acting in Spain must obtain a NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) for non-residents. This is applied through the AEAT before any activity begins, via form 036/036 or through a legal representative resident in Spain when no permanent establishment exists. Temporary/provisional NIFs are issued pending final registration. The application requires proof of incorporation, identity/reference to the home tax ID, certificate of fiscal residence, and designation of representative for tax obligations. For VAT purposes, the same NIF serves as the Spanish VAT ID, supplemented by the territorial code 'N' for non-residents. Cross-border electronic service supplies can alternatively use the simplified VAT One-Stop Shop (OSS, Non-Union Scheme) without a Spanish branch, but a NIF may still be needed for refunds or local compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Spanish law. The SL is categorically a corporate entity subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) at entity level, without pass-through availability. A group of Spanish-resident companies may elect to file under the consolidated corporate tax regime (régimen de consolidación fiscal). Hybrid mismatch elections are constrained by EU ATAD transposition rules, and taxpayers may elect for special regimes such as neutrality in mergers, the holding-company regime (Entidades de Tenencia de Valores Extranjeros), or the patent box regime, as applicable, provided statutory conditions are met.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (IVA – Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover exemption threshold in Spain; any economic activity subject to VAT triggers registration. For intra-EU B2C remote sales of e-services by an established Spanish business, the pan-EU EUR 10,000 (10,000 EUR) threshold applies; below this, the supply is taxed in the establishment country. Non-established foreign digital suppliers generally have no threshold and must register or use the EU Non-Union OSS scheme. Local currency threshold for standard VAT registration: N/A / 0 EUR.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing is mandatory between entrepreneurs and professionals under Spanish commercial law (Ley Crea y Crece); digital game publishers issuing VAT invoices to Spanish businesses must use structured e-invoice formats (factura electrónica) and ensure interoperability. Real-time VAT reporting is compulsory for large taxpayers through the Suministro Inmediato de Información (SII), requiring immediate electronic transmission of invoice details to AEAT databases, mainly through XML/web-service APIs. SII applies to taxpayers with annual turnover above the statutory large-taxpayer threshold and those in certain consolidated/asset situations. No blanket real-time clearance stamping is imposed on all SMEs, but all electronic invoices must be verifiable and readable, and OSS filings are submitted quarterly through the VAT OSS portal. Failure to comply with SII or e-invoice formats triggers penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to non-EU destinations may be zero-rated at 0% VAT if the goods physically leave the EU customs territory and the exporter retains certified evidence of export within the legally required timeframe. For international services, zero-rating or non-taxation in Spain depends on place-of-supply rules: B2B digital services to non-Spanish EU and non-EU business customers are taxable where the customer is established (usually a reverse charge or outside Spanish VAT), while B2C electronic services to non-EU consumers fall outside Spanish VAT entirely; intra-EU B2C e-services are subject to VAT in the consumer's member state via OSS and reported at the applicable foreign VAT rate, not zero-rated. The MMORPG operator should document customer location from at least two non-contradictory pieces of evidence (IP address, bank details, BIC, SIM, fixed-line location).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA/DUE – Documento Único Administrativo/Electrónico)
Commercial Invoice and Sales Contract or equivalent
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing transport leaving EU territory
Proof of receipt by the non-EU importer (arrival certificate or customs clearance in destination)
Inward Remittance Certificate or payment evidence proving foreign currency repatriation
Tax invoice in the required Spanish format with reference to the export/zero-rate exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spanish law provides that exports must be evidenced by customs and transport documentation; false or incomplete documentation triggers immediate VAT assessment and a 10% to 150% late-payment surcharge scale on the uncovered VAT, plus interest. The Spanish Tax Agency may claw back zero-rated supplies for up to 4 years, and misrepresentation to obtain unwarranted 0% VAT or tax refunds is punished with penalties up to 150% of the evaded amount, forfeiture of refund claims, and criminal prosecution under article 305 of the Organic Law on Taxation when amounts exceed statutory thresholds, including imprisonment for serious tax fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) and the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCIIN) of the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism, which jointly supervise foreign exchange operations and capital movements under Spanish Law 19/2003 on Capital Movements and Economic Transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for all current account transactions (payments for goods, services, royalties, salaries) and for capital account transactions. Spain applies full capital liberalisation pursuant to EU Treaty provisions and the OECD Code of Liberalisation. No exchange control approval is required for capital inflows or outflows. However, operations with non-EU jurisdictions exceeding €10,000 per calendar month must be declared to the Banco de España for statistical and monitoring purposes via the R-1 (foreign investment) and R-2 (foreign trade) forms. Profit remittances (dividends) to non-residents are not subject to exchange control but attract 19% withholding tax unless a reduced rate is available under a double tax treaty. No permit or surrender obligation applies to the conversion of export proceeds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no mandatory surrender or forced conversion of export proceeds. Exporters may retain receipts in foreign currency in domestic or foreign accounts and convert freely at market rates. Reporting obligations include: (i) declaration to AEAT (Spanish Tax Agency) for amounts exceeding €10,000 in cash or equivalent, and (ii) statistical declarations to the Banco de España for export collections exceeding €10,000 per transaction per month (Form R-2). These are informational only and do not require approval.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM. EU-regulated electronic money institutions (EMIs) domiciled in Spain or authorised under EU passporting (e.g., BaaS providers, Revolut Business, N26) can be used for ancillary treasury operations such as small-volume payouts and travel expenses. They are NOT recommended for capital escrow, large intercompany loans, or accumulating export proceeds due to lower AML thresholds and potential regulatory friction. Non-EU offshore EMIs (e.g., UK-based after Brexit) are subject to re-authorisation under the Spanish payment services regime; operating without a branch or agent may cause legal invalidity. For a hardcore MMORPG publisher relying on high-volume app-store payouts, an EMI can serve as a secondary receiving account, but the primary clearing account must be a tier-1 commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly incorporated Spanish SL with non-resident shareholders or directors, physical presence of the legal representative (CEO, CFO) or an appointed attorney-in-fact is required to sign the account opening mandate and complete enhanced due diligence. Some banks permit remote video-onboarding if the company has been operating for more than one year and presents audited financials; for start-ups, a physical interview at the registered branch is typically mandatory. The physical attendance requirement applies at least to one member of the board; other beneficial owners may complete remote KYC if their identity is properly notarised and apostilled.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction velocity from app stores with small ticket items (USD 0.99 – 9.99) from diverse countries, flagged as possible money laundering smurfing or trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Official contracts with Apple App Store and Google Play proof of publisher account, including developer ID, revenue share schedules. (2) Monthly payout statements from Apple/Google showing aggregated user payments and tax deductions. (3) Audited financial statements of the SL. (4) A written AML risk assessment of the business model, concluding low risk without cash redemption. (5) Transactional logs reasonably aggregated, proving no structuring of amounts or velocity indicative of smurfing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner or controlling shareholder residing in a high-risk or non-cooperative jurisdiction (e.g., FATF grey list) or with prior adverse media exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Valid passport and tax residency certificate of the beneficial owner. (2) Professional reference letters from a licensed legal/accounting firm in Spain. (3) Court records or an independent background screening report from a reputable compliance provider. (4) Justification of the source of funds for capital injection (e.g., sale of token, prior employment). (5) Evidence of economic substance in Spain: registered office lease, 2-5 local employees, and Spanish tax registrations (NIE, CIF, AEAT with activity code 5820).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected inbound transfers from related foreign entities without proper intercompany documentation, triggering anti-concealment scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Signed intercompany loan or service agreement, including transfer pricing documentation under OECD Chapter V. (2) Spanish corporate income tax form 232 (related-party statement) if the transfer exceeds €250,000. (3) Director's resolution approving the transaction. (4) Bank beneficiary/remitter full legal names and account numbers. (5) A statement of purpose codes for each transfer (investment, loan, payment for services).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fast-growing revenue from app stores without corresponding local commercial substance (shell company red flag).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Detailed business plan for the Spanish entity including headcount, local marketing, game-development services, and server hosting. (2) Employment contracts with Spanish-resident staff and social security registration. (3) Invoices to third parties for services rendered. (4) Any patent, trademark, or domain registrations held by the SL. (5) A letter from a Spanish notary confirming the SL is not a shell but an operating entity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All capital injections into the Spanish SL must be executed via SWIFT MT103 (or equivalent) using the ISO 20022 wire message format with proper purpose code. For equity contributions from non-EU shareholders, use 'EQUI' (equity increase) or 'DINV' (direct investment) under the BOP reporting codes. The beneficiary bank will require a copy of the shareholder meeting minutes approving the capital increase and the notarised public deed (Escritura Pública). If the investment exceeds €3,005,000, prior filing with the DGCIIN is required (Form D-7). For any transfer exceeding €10,000, simultaneous declaration to the Banco de España (Form R-1) is mandatory; this can be done by the bank in most cases. To facilitate onboarding, the bank will request: (i) certificate of the SL's tax identification number (NIF), (ii) certificate of directors, (iii) passport copies of foreign investors, and (iv) proof of address of the shareholder for non-EU residents.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: International trade disbursements for a gaming company (e.g., payments to overseas developers, cloud hosting providers, advertising agencies) should be cleared through: (a) SWIFT MT103 direct transfers for amounts below EUR 1 million, with proper purpose codes such as 'PROS' (professional services) or 'ROYA' (royalties) for license fees; (b) SEPA Instant or SEPA Credit Transfer for EU counterparties up to EUR 100,000; (c) Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) are generally not used for digital services, but may be considered for substantial software licensing contracts exceeding EUR 5 million where the counterparty requires payment guarantee; (d) For recurring mass payouts, use the commercial bank's host-to-host H2H interface or API treasury automation to route payments with full reconciliation. All outbound transfers require supporting invoices or contracts to satisfy AEAT anti-fraud checks; non-documentary transfers above €10,000 must be declared to the Banco de España (Form R-2).
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Outright Forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CNY) with physical or cash settlement, maturities up to 12 months, subject to ISDA or bank master agreement.
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for currencies with limited convertibility (e.g., BRL, ARS, TRY) used to hedge emerging-market revenues, cash-settled offshore.
Cross-Currency Swaps (fixed-to-fixed or floating-to-fixed) for managing long-term liquidity mismatches between EUR-denominated costs and USD/JPY-denominated revenue streams.
FX Currency Options (call and put) to hedge contingent exposure from future app-store payouts, purchased OTC from tier-1 banks with pre-approved credit lines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 4 months after the end of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to €3,000; possible administrative strike-off for repeated non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 25 days after the end of the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties up to €1,500 plus interest; risk of tax reassessment and audits

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the SL exceeds two of the following: net turnover > €20 million, total assets > €10 million, or average number of employees > 50
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (PGC) or International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No mandatory annual confirmation required; beneficial owner register must be updated within one month of any change in shareholding or control

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general Spanish corporate income tax rate. Qualifying newly created entities generally apply 15% in the first tax period in which they obtain a positive taxable base and the following tax period, subject to statutory exclusions. For tax periods beginning in 2025, qualifying micro-enterprises with net turnover below EUR 1 million apply 17% on the first EUR 50,000 of taxable income and 20% on the remainder; qualifying small entities below EUR 10 million generally apply 24%. Rates and transitional rules depend on tax period and entity eligibility.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Potential relief includes the 15% start-up rate, reduced rates for qualifying micro-enterprises and small entities, deductions for qualifying R&D and technological innovation, and deductions for qualifying audiovisual productions and certain cultural investments. Incentive eligibility, limits, documentation, and interaction with minimum-tax rules must be checked for each tax period. Spain has no general corporate income tax holiday.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited; Spanish tax losses generally do not expire. Utilization is subject to annual quantitative limits, minimum utilization rules, anti-trafficking restrictions, and other statutory conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, corporate income tax self-assessment, filed electronically through the Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT) electronic office using an accepted electronic certificate or other authorized authentication.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the usual filing window is 1–25 July of the following year, subject to calendar and filing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify the SL by Spanish tax identification number, legal name, tax address, tax period start and end dates, and applicable tax regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned Spanish SL files as a Spanish-resident corporate taxpayer. Identify foreign shareholders where requested; non-resident ownership does not change the SL's residence or filing obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the principal activity, applicable accounting framework, balance-sheet and profit-and-loss information, and relevant accounting and tax status indicators.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish entity's own accounts and Spanish tax identifiers. Do not report the foreign shareholder's worldwide accounts as the SL's accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile accounting profit or loss to the corporate income tax base, including non-deductible expenses, exempt income, tax adjustments, impairment, depreciation, and other statutory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Spanish tax law to the SL's income and expenses. Separately analyze cross-border related-party charges, permanent-establishment issues, and withholding taxes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report available tax-loss carryforwards and claimed deductions, with supporting schedules and applicable limitation calculations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain evidence of the losses and deductions at the Spanish entity level. Ownership changes and changes in activity can restrict loss utilization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax rate and gross tax liability
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the rate applicable to the tax period and taxpayer, including any qualifying reduced rate, and calculate gross liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign shareholder does not by itself qualify the SL for a reduced rate. Substantiate all rate-specific conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim permitted deductions, tax credits, Spanish withholdings, and payments on account, reconciling them to supporting certificates and filed payment forms.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only amounts attributable to the SL and supported by Spanish tax certificates or payment records; do not claim a shareholder's foreign tax credits as the SL's credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Final assessment and payment or refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the balance payable or refundable, select the applicable payment or refund method, and submit the return electronically.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use a Spanish-authorized payment method or valid Spanish bank account where required. A foreign shareholder should arrange payment authority and electronic representation before the deadline.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without prior request generally attracts a surcharge of 1% plus 1% for each full month of delay; after 12 months, the surcharge is generally 15%, with late-payment interest potentially accruing after the 12-month period. If the AEAT has issued a prior request, failure to file can constitute a tax infringement, generally penalized at 50%–150% of the unpaid amount, subject to statutory aggravating and reduction rules. Incorrect returns can attract separate penalties. Late payment may also incur surcharges and interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, corporate income tax instalment payment, submitted electronically through the AEAT electronic office.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Generally three instalments per tax period, in April, October, and December, subject to the statutory filing windows and applicable payment method.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally within the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December. The required calculation method depends on the taxpayer's circumstances; certain taxpayers must use the current-period taxable-base method.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify the SL, tax period, instalment period, and applicable calculation method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File for the Spanish SL under its Spanish tax identification number, regardless of the residence of its shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the payment using the statutory method applicable to the taxpayer, based on prior-period liability or current-period taxable income, as applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the SL's Spanish tax figures and apply any mandatory current-period method. Do not use the foreign parent's tax liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the amount payable and complete the electronic payment or other permitted settlement procedure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the Spanish entity or its authorized representative has funds and payment authority available by the deadline.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted instalment payments may result in late-payment surcharges, interest, and, where the conduct meets the statutory infringement criteria, penalties. The amount depends on whether the payment is voluntary or follows an AEAT request and on the applicable Tax General Law provisions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish domestic withholding tax generally applies to dividends paid to non-resident shareholders, subject to statutory exemptions and treaty relief. Qualifying EU parent companies may obtain an exemption under the Parent-Subsidiary regime, generally subject to a minimum 5% holding, a one-year holding or commitment condition, qualifying legal form and tax-subjection conditions, and anti-abuse rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the recipient should provide the Spanish payer with a valid tax residence certificate issued by the competent authority of the treaty jurisdiction and the documentation required to establish beneficial ownership and satisfaction of treaty conditions. The payer applies the treaty rate where the Spanish rules and documentation permit; otherwise it generally withholds domestically and the recipient may seek a refund from the AEAT using the applicable non-resident refund procedure. Certificates should cover the relevant payment period and be renewed as required. Treaty entitlement remains subject to limitation-on-benefits, principal-purpose, beneficial-ownership, and anti-abuse provisions where applicable.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The general Spanish domestic non-resident withholding rate on Spanish-source interest and royalties paid to non-residents is generally 19%, subject to domestic exemptions and classification rules. The EU Interest and Royalties Directive may provide an exemption for qualifying associated companies meeting its ownership, legal-form, tax-subjection, and holding-period conditions. Tax treaties commonly reduce source-country rates, but the applicable rate depends on the recipient's residence, beneficial ownership, treaty text, and any applicable anti-abuse rule. Payments to non-resident entities should be analyzed for Spanish-source status and treaty eligibility before payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Spanish documentation rules generally require related-party transaction documentation, subject to statutory exemptions and simplifications. The principal documentation exemption commonly applies where the aggregate consideration for related-party transactions with the same related person does not exceed EUR 250,000 in the tax period, subject to exceptions. Master File preparation is generally required for qualifying groups with consolidated net turnover of at least EUR 45 million. Local File requirements and simplified-documentation eligibility depend on group size, transaction type, and statutory exclusions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not have a separate general Economic Substance Regulations regime equivalent to certain offshore jurisdictions. Spanish tax law nevertheless applies transfer-pricing rules, beneficial-ownership requirements, residence and permanent-establishment principles, general anti-abuse provisions, and specific anti-hybrid and controlled-foreign-company rules. A Spanish SL should maintain evidence that its functions, assets, personnel, decision-making, and risks support its reported income and deductions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion, concealed income, or materially false corporate tax returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional concealment of revenue, fictitious expenses, false invoices, fraudulent deductions, or other conduct causing an unlawful tax shortfall.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax infringements can attract administrative penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, depending on the infringement and aggravating circumstances. Conduct meeting the criminal threshold under the Spanish Criminal Code may result in imprisonment and criminal fines; the basic tax-fraud offense generally requires the statutory threshold of more than EUR 120,000 per tax and tax period, subject to offense-specific rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil or tax liability where statutory conditions are met, including liability for participation, culpable non-compliance, or failure to act during insolvency. Criminally responsible individuals may face imprisonment and fines. Travel restrictions are not an automatic tax penalty and require a separate legal basis or judicial order.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Related-party pricing and undocumented intercompany transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing game-development services, IP licenses, platform support, financing, or other controlled transactions outside the arm's-length standard, or failing to maintain required supporting documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT may adjust taxable income and assess tax, late-payment interest, and penalties. Failure to provide or maintain required transfer-pricing documentation can trigger specific fixed and proportional penalties under Spanish tax law; the amount depends on the breach, transaction value, and resulting adjustment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatically personally liable for a transfer-pricing adjustment. Personal exposure may arise for intentional participation, serious or repeated tax infringements, or statutory grounds for subsidiary liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper dividend, interest, or royalty withholding
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Applying a treaty or EU exemption without valid residence, beneficial-ownership, holding, or anti-abuse evidence; failing to withhold or remit tax; or mischaracterizing a distribution as a deductible payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Spanish payer may be assessed for unwithheld tax, interest, and applicable penalties. Treaty relief denied to the recipient may also result in a refund claim being rejected or tax being assessed under the domestic rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face subsidiary liability where statutory conditions are met, including culpable failure to comply with withholding obligations. Criminal liability requires satisfaction of the relevant criminal-law elements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell arrangements, sham transactions, or abusive treaty access
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Spanish SL without genuine commercial activity or decision-making to obtain treaty benefits, route income, create artificial deductions, or disguise the beneficial owner or actual recipient.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT may deny treaty or statutory benefits, recharacterize transactions, assess tax and interest, and impose applicable penalties. Criminal sanctions may apply if the facts satisfy a criminal offense.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A company's limited liability is not automatically displaced. Personal civil, tax, or criminal liability requires an applicable statutory basis, such as fraud, culpable conduct, abuse of legal personality, or participation in an offense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly concealing, converting, transferring, or possessing criminal proceeds, or failing to comply with applicable anti-money-laundering obligations where the SL or its activities fall within regulated-person requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Spanish anti-money-laundering law provides administrative sanctions for covered breaches, including fines and potential restrictions. Money laundering is a criminal offense and may result in imprisonment, fines, and confiscation under the Criminal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals who knowingly participate may face criminal prosecution, imprisonment, fines, and confiscation. Directors may also face administrative consequences where they are responsible for a covered entity's compliance failures. Travel bans are not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to maintain books, records, or supporting evidence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to keep reliable accounting records, retain tax and transfer-pricing evidence, or produce records requested by the AEAT, including records supporting app-store settlements, digital sales, refunds, and related-party IP charges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Consequences may include tax-base adjustments, denial of deductions, information-reporting or accounting penalties, late-payment interest, and penalties for obstruction or failure to provide required information, as applicable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal consequences where they intentionally obstruct an investigation, participate in fraud, or satisfy statutory criteria for subsidiary liability; ordinary recordkeeping errors do not automatically pierce limited liability.
